uncited: - Input: Set of Gaussian primitives $\mathcal{G}$, current iteration $t$, pruning threshold $\tau$, pruning interval $I_{prune}$, vote threshold $v$.
Each Gaussian $g$ has attributes: opacity $o_g$, scale vector $\mathbf{s}_g$ (or maximum scale $s_{max}(g)$), position, rotation, spherical harmonics coefficients.
**Accumulate Votes:** Update the vote count for each Gaussian.
**Prune:** Check if any Gaussian has accumulated enough votes to be permanently removed.
A larger threshold results in more aggressive pruning.
Value not explicitly given in the main definition section, but used in the threshold calculation.

If $g \in \mathcal{C}_{\text{prune}}^{(t)}$, increment its vote count [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the set of pruning candidates is defined as $C_{prune}^{(t)}$. It further defines the update rule for the vote count $V_g^{(t)}$ as $V_g^{(t+1)} = V_g^{(t)} + 1_{g in C_{prune}^{(t)}}$, which mathematically means that if a Gaussian $g$ is in the set $C_{prune}^{(t)}$, its vote count is incremented by 1. This directly supports the claim.

It identifies pruning candidates $\mathcal{C}_{\text{prune}}^{(t)}$ based on opacity and scale criteria, updates vote counts $V_g^{(t+1)} = V_g^{(t)} + \mathbf{1}_{\{g \in \mathcal{C}_{\text{prune}}^{(t)}\}}$, and permanently prunes Gaussians $g$ where $V_g^{(t)} > I_{prune} \cdot v$ [S1, unofficial].

The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly supports every component of the claim: 1) It identifies pruning candidates based on opacity and scale criteria (Section 3.3, Eq 7). 2) It updates vote counts using the formula $V_g^{(t+1)} = V_g^{(t)} + 1_{g in C_{prune}^{(t)}}$ (Section 3.3, Eq 8). 3) It permanently prunes Gaussians where the accumulated votes exceed the threshold defined by the pruning interval and vote threshold ($V_g^{(t)} > I_{prune} * v$) (Section 3.3, Eq 8 and Implementation section). All mathematical notations and logical steps match the claim.
